Shir l'Tsiyōn — a hymn celebrating the reïfication of the Balfour Declaration at the culmination of the San Remo conference on 11 May 1920 by Rabbi Jacob Gerstein

tei:bibl.tei:title: שִׁיר לְצִיּוֹן
Shir l'Tsiyōn — a hymn celebrating the reïfication of the Balfour Declaration at the culmination of the San Remo conference on 11 May 1920 by Rabbi Jacob Gerstein
tei:bibl.tei:author: Jacob Gerstein
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: In this song written in rhymed Yiddish verse, Rabbi Gerstein celebrates the day of 11 May 1920, the date upon which determined the fate of the Ottoman Empire after World War I was concluded and the Balfour Declaration of 1917 reïfied in favor of Jewish national objectives in the Land of Israel.

This is “Shir lə-Tsiyōn” by Rabbi Jacob Gerstein, first published in 1920. Many thanks to Shulamith Z. Berger, Curator of Special Collections at Yeshiva University), for sharing the existence of this song in the context of the San Remo conference, and for pointing us to the archival resource from which I prepared this transcription. It appears on the last page of “Various liturgical compositions, manuscript 151.” I also prepared the English translation of the Yiddish. –Aharon Varady
